original_test_intent: Verify that the product FRU contains the approved finished-system part number/SKU and that the authoritative BMC UI/OEM inventory reports the same product identity.
original_method: Bind the product FRU and UI/API resource, securely retrieve raw part-number values, apply only approved punctuation and revision/SKU rules, and compare them with the versioned product BOM or orderable-part record.
manual_activity: Supply the authoritative product part number/SKU, product-resource mapping and approved revision/format policy; no physical or state-changing action is required.
required_inputs: Authoritative product part number/SKU and revision
Approved punctuation, whitespace and suffix policy
safety_requirements: Use read-only FRU and API operations
Never write FRU or issue raw mutation/PATCH/product control
Do not substitute board or chassis PN
Preserve raw SKU and revision tokens
Do not strip option/revision suffixes without approval
Stop on multiple product records or SKU ambiguity
agent_execution_scope: Bind the intended product FRU record
Resolve the validated OEM/UI product resource
Capture complete redacted evidence and statuses
Report exact mismatch or unresolved suffix
engineer_actions: Supply the expected product PN/SKU and revision
Resolve obsolete or customer-specific SKU differences

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `ipmitool fru print` can expose Product Part Number, but the assumed `.Product.PartNumber` under `/Chassis/system` is not validated. A raw string view or missing-path fallback cannot prove the correct SKU/revision and may select a component PN instead.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use secure read-only access to capture the bound product FRU and validated OEM/UI product PartNumber, preserve raw SKU/revision tokens and compare them with the approved product BOM/orderable-part record under explicit formatting rules.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The `ipmitool fru list` inspection, Product Part Number field, UI agreement criterion and 2/0-minute timing are preserved; resource, oracle and revision rules are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a product-scoped comparator that records FRU/resource provenance, raw part-number tokens, option/revision suffixes, BOM/SKU reference and normalization-policy version.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds product-level identity and orderable-part provenance instead of assuming an arbitrary JSON property represents the correct SKU.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects wrong finished-product SKU, option code and revision while retaining the intended read-only FRU/UI comparison.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Customer-specific or option suffixes can be material; overly broad normalization can accept the wrong configured product.

project_override_considerations: Product Part Number is distinct from Board Part Number and Chassis Part Number. Unavailable private script behavior cannot be used to infer equivalence among these identities.
expected_evidence: Selected product FRU and OEM/UI resource
Complete redacted raw responses and statuses
Raw product PN/SKU and revision tokens
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master and prior reviews consistently target Product Part Number. Missing product mapping, expected SKU and revision semantics are execution gaps, not conflicting source meaning.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The product/SKU field and comparison are clear. The BOM oracle, source mapping and suffix policy are finite project packages.

review_improvement: Prevents a board/chassis PN, guessed API property or stripped SKU suffix from being accepted as proof of the finished product's part number.
independent_technical_reasoning: Product Part Number usually identifies an orderable configured system, while board and chassis part numbers identify subassemblies. Option and revision suffixes can encode customer configuration or regulatory differences, so they cannot be discarded casually. The comparison must be tied to the product FRU/resource and orderable-part oracle. Because these are identifiable data packages for a read-only check, REQUIRES is appropriate and BLOCKED is unnecessary.
